newsitem.title: CHINA: China, U.S. textile talks continue on fourth day.
newsitem.headline: China, U.S. textile talks continue on fourth day.

text.p: Chinese and U.S. textile negotiators on Thursday wrangled into the night in talks to end a dispute over millions of dollars of penalties imposed by Washington on Chinese imports.
"They are still in session," a U.S. embassy official said late on Thursday, the last day of a scheduled four days of textile talks in the Chinese capital that began on Monday.

Washington's top textile negotiator Rita Hayes was discussing a new Sino-U.S textile agreement during talks with China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as well as trying to end the textile imports dispute.
The embassy official declined to comment on how the talks were progressing or how long they would continue, but said Hayes was scheduled to leave Beijing on Friday morning.
The United States last September set penalties of $19 million on Chinese imports, saying Beijing was shipping textiles through third countries to avoid quota restrictions.
China has threatened to retaliate by temporarily banning imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks, with the curbs to go into effect on December 10.
The two sides must also agree to extend textile cooperation by concluding a new agreement to replace the current textile pact that expires at the end of the year, officials say.
China's huge textile sales to the United States have long been a sensitive point for U.S. trade negotiators eager to reduce Wasington's swelling trade deficit.

Washington says its 1995 trade deficit with China was worth $35 billion, making trade a major issue in ties already strained by disagreement over Taiwan, weapons sales, nuclear proliferation and copyright piracy.
